title: Dual-Issue Execution of Mixed Integer and Floating-Point Workloads on Energy-Efficient In-Order RISC-V Cores
problem: Single-issue in-order cores have limited instruction-level parallelism (IPC); dual-issue cores offer potential performance boost but with increased area and energy overhead. Mixed integer and floating-point workloads are common but underserved.
motivation: General-purpose accelerator architectures need extremely area- and energy-efficient processing elements; lean dual-issue cores can improve throughput on mixed-type workloads.
method: Develops COPIFT methodology and RISC-V ISA extensions enabling low-cost dual-issue execution of mixed integer and floating-point instruction sequences. The approach couples integer and floating-point functional units to reduce area overhead while maintaining timing, leveraging instruction-type diversity to achieve parallelism.
key_novelty: First methodology for lean dual-issue RISC-V cores with ISA extensions for efficient mixed integer-FP execution.
contributions: COPIFT methodology for dual-issue mixed integer-FP execution
RISC-V ISA extensions enabling lean dual-issue architecture
1.47x speedup on mixed kernels, 1.75 peak IPC, 1.37x energy improvement vs. RV32G baselines
primary_theme: Lean dual-issue RISC-V for mixed integer-FP workloads
